title: Rework Plex metadata provider around strict contract
description: Refactor sportscanner2's Plex custom metadata provider to follow the working plex-meta-tvdb architectural pattern while preserving SportScanner's sports-specific metadata behavior. Scope: restore Plex-compliant MediaProvider contract, split route/match/metadata concerns, validate response models, and add regression coverage including live Plex contract checks where feasible.

title: Audit Plex metadata provider spec compliance
description: Review sportscanner2 against the official Plex Metadata Providers specification and fix any compliance gaps found while validating the provider and match endpoints.

title: Add tests that validate loaded event metadata against TheSportsDB
description: Current deterministic workflow coverage uses ScenarioMetadataSource in sportscanner2/src/sportscanner/testing/workflow_harness.py, so it can pass while only asserting titles that the application itself injected. Add test coverage that exercises the TheSportsDB-backed metadata path and verifies the metadata exposed for loaded events matches the expected TheSportsDB event data, especially event titles, instead of arbitrary application-defined names. Scope should likely include either a fixture-backed TheSportsDB client/adapter path or an integration-style metadata assertion through the provider endpoints after ingest. Acceptance criteria: (1) at least one loaded event is validated against expected TheSportsDB event metadata, (2) the test would fail if the app substituted its own title instead of the upstream event title, and (3) the coverage is documented well enough to extend for more competitions later.

title: Make clean Sport_Test scans switch Plex episodes off local metadata
description: The strengthened live test for SportScanner-8k0 now cleans its own live-plex artifacts, deletes only stale Formula 1 live-test metadata from the dedicated Sport_Test library, and asserts the stored Plex item switches from local:// GUIDs to the SportScanner provider GUID/title/date. On 2026-03-10, the live test reproduced the underlying failure after a clean scan: Plex scans the file into Sport_Test, but the episode never leaves local metadata even though /provider/tv/library/metadata/episode_<segment_id> returns the expected SportScanner payload. Investigate the Plex-side matching/refresh path needed for clean Sport_Test scans to apply provider-backed metadata.

title: Improve staged/review workflow for unmatched episodes
description: The current review flow is too limited when SportScanner cannot determine what an episode should match against. Right now the user can review staged items, but if no usable match candidates exist the only available action is effectively to publish as a special. Track a better workflow that lets the user identify the correct competition/event/season destination more accurately, with explicit controls for selecting or searching the intended target instead of forcing a special-case fallback.

title: Make Sport_Test show real TheSportsDB metadata during testing
description: In the live Sport_Test testing flow, Plex currently scans SportScanner-published files into the library but leaves the items on generic local metadata instead of showing the expected SportScanner/TheSportsDB-backed titles, dates, and other resolved metadata. Track the work needed to make the Sport_Test test workflow verify that Plex actually displays the real metadata downloaded from TheSportsDB during testing, not just that files are scanned and provider metadata is available.
close_reason: Implemented the live Sport_Test verification path so the test now cleans its own artifacts and asserts Plex stores provider-backed metadata; opened SportScanner-y9h for the newly exposed Plex-side matching failure.

title: [bug] Episode title match scoring ignores display title — only checks segment.title
description:
In `_match_episode_items()`, when `payload.title` is set, the code scores candidates with:
```python
title_score = sequence_score(payload.title, segment.title)
```
`segment.title` is the short title parsed from the filename (e.g. `"Qualifying"`). But Plex often sends `payload.title` equal to the full display title it already knows (e.g. `"Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` or `"Australian Grand Prix Qualifying"`). `similarity("Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying", "Qualifying")` ≈ 0.35 — below the 60-point cutoff — so the segment is discarded and the match fails.

This particularly affects re-match attempts and cases where Plex sends a title-only match request without `index` or `date`.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/provider/match_service.py`

**Dependency:** SportScanner-acb must be implemented first — `episode_display_title()` must accept `competition_name` parameter before this fix calls it with that argument.

**`episode_display_title` is already imported** in this file:
```python
from sportscanner.provider.items import (
    dedupe_metadata,
    episode_metadata,
    season_metadata,
    segment_event_dates,
    sequence_score,
    show_metadata,
    with_score,
)
```
No new imports required.

**Change — restructure the title-scoring block inside `_match_episode_items()`.**

Find the end of the per-segment scoring loop (inside the `for segment in segments:` loop). The current code is approximately:
```python
                if payload.title:
                    title_score = sequence_score(payload.title, segment.title)
                    if title_score < 60 and payload.index is None and payload.date is None:
                        continue
                    score = max(score, min(100, title_score))
                event = session.get(Event, segment.event_id) if segment.event_id else None
                items.append((score, segment, season, competition, event))
```
Replace with:
```python
                event = session.get(Event, segment.event_id) if segment.event_id else None
                if payload.title:
                    display_title = episode_display_title(segment, event, competition.name)
                    title_score = max(
                        sequence_score(payload.title, segment.title),
                        sequence_score(payload.title, display_title),
                    )
                    if title_score < 60 and payload.index is None and payload.date is None:
                        continue
                    score = max(score, min(100, title_score))
                items.append((score, segment, season, competition, event))
```

Key points:
- `event` is fetched **before** the title check (moved up by one block) so it is available to `episode_display_title`. Previously `event` was fetched on the last line before `items.append`; moving it two lines earlier is safe — it was unconditionally fetched before anyway.
- `display_title` is the cleaned episode title (e.g. `"Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"`) that Plex would have received from the metadata endpoint. Scoring against both `segment.title` and `display_title` means the match succeeds whether Plex sends the short or long form.
- The filter threshold (60) and score cap (100) are unchanged.

**Verification:**
Construct a scenario:
- `segment.title = "Qualifying"`, `segment.kind = "qualifying"`
- `event.name = "2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"`
- `competition.name = "Formula 1"`
- `payload.title = "Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` (the display title Plex knows)
- `payload.index = None`, `payload.date = None`

Before fix: `sequence_score("Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying", "Qualifying")` ≈ 35 → filtered out.
After fix: `display_title = "Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"`, `sequence_score("Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying", "Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying")` = 100 → kept, score set to 100.
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: episode matching now scores both the short local segment title and the cleaned provider display title, which fixes title-only rematches from Plex. Added provider match regression coverage.

title: [feature] Support event_order in competition.sportscanner.yml config file
description:
`_apply_competition_config()` in `service.py` reads a `competition.sportscanner.yml` file placed at or above the file's directory and applies recognised fields to the Competition DB row. Currently only `season_pattern`, `season_split_month`, `season_split_day` are handled. The `event_order` field is silently ignored.

For F1, `event_order` must be `"weekend"` so that all sessions of a race weekend (FP1, FP2, Qualifying, Race) group together and get sequential episode numbers. There is currently no way to set this via config — the user must directly update the DB row. Fix by adding `event_order` support.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/organizer/service.py`

**Change 1 — add `EventOrder` to the db.models import line.**

Find:
```python
from sportscanner.db.models import Competition, CompetitionSeason, Event, EventOrigin, ReviewTask, ReviewTaskStatus, Segment, SegmentStatus
```
Add `EventOrder`:
```python
from sportscanner.db.models import Competition, CompetitionSeason, Event, EventOrder, EventOrigin, ReviewTask, ReviewTaskStatus, Segment, SegmentStatus
```

**Change 2 — extend `_apply_competition_config()`.**

Find the method (it currently ends after `season_split_day` block). Add the `event_order` block at the end:
```python
    def _apply_competition_config(self, competition: Competition, source_path: Path) -> None:
        config = read_competition_config(source_path)
        if not config:
            return
        if config.get("season_pattern"):
            competition.season_pattern = config["season_pattern"]
        if config.get("season_split_month"):
            competition.season_split_month = int(config["season_split_month"])
        if config.get("season_split_day"):
            competition.season_split_day = int(config["season_split_day"])
        if config.get("event_order"):
            raw = config["event_order"].lower()
            valid_orders = {e.value for e in EventOrder}
            if raw in valid_orders:
                competition.event_order = raw
            else:
                logger.warning(
                    "competition_config_invalid_event_order competition=%s value=%s valid=%s",
                    competition.name, raw, sorted(valid_orders),
                )
```

**No other changes required.**

**How the config file looks for F1** — create this file at the root incoming directory that contains F1 files (e.g. `/Volumes/data/incoming/Formula 1/competition.sportscanner.yml`):
```yaml
event_order: weekend
```
Valid values are whatever `EventOrder` enum defines — check `src/sportscanner/db/models.py` for the enum; currently `"official"`, `"weekend"`, `"round"`.

**Verification:**
1. Create `competition.sportscanner.yml` with `event_order: weekend` in the F1 incoming dir.
2. Ingest any F1 file from that directory.
3. Query: `SELECT event_order FROM competition WHERE name = 'Formula 1';` → should be `"weekend"`.
4. Test invalid value: `event_order: banana` → warning logged, competition.event_order unchanged.
5. Test case-insensitivity: `event_order: WEEKEND` → `.lower()` normalises to `"weekend"` → accepted.
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: added event_order support in competition.sportscanner.yml with enum validation and warning logs; also aligned weekend sequencing so weekend mode assigns one event sequence per weekend group. Added organizer and numbering coverage.

title: [bug] event.weekend_group is never persisted to DB — always NULL
description:
`_upsert_event()` in `service.py` sets `event.weekend_group = upstream.weekend_group`. However, `upstream.weekend_group` is always `None` because the TheSportsDB adapter (`adapter.py`) never populates that field in `UpstreamEvent`. The `Event.weekend_group` DB column is therefore always `NULL` after ingest.

`compute_event_sequences()` in `weekend` mode does call `derive_weekend_group(item.weekend_group or item.name)`, so it falls back to computing the group from the event name on every sequence recompute. This means sequencing itself works — but the stored column is meaningless, admin UI queries on it return nothing, and any future feature relying on the stored group will break.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/organizer/service.py`

**Change 1 — add `derive_weekend_group` to the numbering import line.**

Find the existing import:
```python
from sportscanner.organizer.numbering import EventSequenceInput, SegmentCodeInput, compute_event_sequences, compute_segment_codes, episode_number
```
Add `derive_weekend_group` to it:
```python
from sportscanner.organizer.numbering import EventSequenceInput, SegmentCodeInput, compute_event_sequences, compute_segment_codes, derive_weekend_group, episode_number
```

**Change 2 — in `_upsert_event()`, replace the weekend_group assignment line.**

Find (inside `_upsert_event`):
```python
        event.weekend_group = upstream.weekend_group
```
Replace with:
```python
        event.weekend_group = upstream.weekend_group or derive_weekend_group(upstream.name)
```

That is the only change required. The rest of `_upsert_event()` stays identical. Do NOT modify the adapter (`thesportsdb/adapter.py`) — keep the `UpstreamEvent.weekend_group` field as `None` from the adapter so that explicit sidecar-provided weekend groups (set via manual override) are still respected: `upstream.weekend_group or derive_weekend_group(...)` only calls the fallback when the field is falsy.

**Verification:**
After ingesting an F1 season event, query:
```sql
SELECT name, weekend_group FROM event WHERE competition_season_id = '<season_id>';
```
All sessions of the Australian GP weekend should have `weekend_group = "formula 1 australian grand prix"` (the output of `derive_weekend_group("2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Free Practice 1")` etc. — see bead SportScanner-ld4 for derive_weekend_group expected outputs).

**Dependency:** This bead depends on SportScanner-ld4 (`derive_weekend_group` must be updated first) to produce correct group strings.
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: event.weekend_group is now persisted via upstream.weekend_group or derive_weekend_group(upstream.name). Added sidecar lookup coverage proving the derived value is stored.

title: [bug] derive_weekend_group does not strip year prefix from TheSportsDB event names
description:
`derive_weekend_group()` in `numbering.py` strips inline session-type words from event names to produce a "weekend" grouping key. The `compute_event_sequences()` function uses this key when `event_order == "weekend"` to assign the same sequence number to all sessions of the same race weekend (FP1, FP2, Qualifying, Race all get sequence 1 for Australian GP, then sequence 2 for Chinese GP, etc.).

**The problem:** The function strips session keywords but not the leading year token ("2025 "). For TheSportsDB F1 event names:
- `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Free Practice 1"` → strips "free practice 1" → `"2025 formula 1 australian grand prix"`
- `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix"` (race) → strips nothing → `"2025 formula 1 australian grand prix"`

These match, so weekend grouping works **if** naming is consistent. But it breaks if some events have the year prefix and others don't, or if a race event has a slightly different name format. Fix for robustness.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/organizer/numbering.py`

**Change 1 — add two module-level regex constants** near the top of the file (after `_LATE_DATE`/`_LATE_TIME`):
```python
_YEAR_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}(?:/\d{2,4})?\s+")
_DASH_SESSION_SUFFIX_RE = re.compile(
    r"\s*[-–]\s*\b(?:free\s+practice\s*\d*|fp\d+|practice\s*\d*|"
    r"sprint\s+qualifying|sprint\s+race|sprint|qualifying|qual|race|"
    r"pregame|postgame|highlights|analysis|condensed)\b.*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

**Change 2 — rewrite `derive_weekend_group()`:**

Old function (lines 36–44):
```python
def derive_weekend_group(name: str) -> str:
    normalized = normalize_title(name)
    normalized = re.sub(
        r"\b(practice\s*\d+|fp\d+|qualifying|sprint qualifying|sprint|race|pregame|postgame|highlights|analysis|condensed)\b",
        "",
        normalized,
    )
    normalized = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", normalized).strip()
    return normalized or normalize_title(name)
```
New function:
```python
def derive_weekend_group(name: str) -> str:
    # Step 1: strip leading "YYYY " or "YYYY/YY " year token
    text = _YEAR_PREFIX_RE.sub("", name).strip()
    # Step 2: strip dash-separated session suffix ("Australian GP - Free Practice 1")
    text = _DASH_SESSION_SUFFIX_RE.sub("", text).strip()
    # Step 3: strip any remaining inline session keywords (original behaviour)
    normalized = normalize_title(text)
    normalized = re.sub(
        r"\b(free\s+practice\s*\d*|fp\d+|practice\s*\d+|practice|"
        r"sprint\s+qualifying|sprint\s+race|sprint|qualifying|qual|race|"
        r"pregame|postgame|highlights|analysis|condensed)\b",
        "",
        normalized,
    )
    normalized = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", normalized).strip()
    return normalized or normalize_title(name)
```

**Important:** `re` is already imported in `numbering.py` (used by `normalize_title`). No new import needed.

**Verification:**
| Input | Expected output |
|---|---|
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Free Practice 1"` | `"formula 1 australian grand prix"` |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Sprint Race"` | `"formula 1 australian grand prix"` |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` | `"formula 1 australian grand prix"` |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix"` | `"formula 1 australian grand prix"` |
| `"Monaco Grand Prix Practice 1"` (no year) | `"monaco grand prix"` |
| `"Arsenal vs Bournemouth"` | `"arsenal vs bournemouth"` (no session keywords) |
| `"2025/26 Premier League Chelsea vs Arsenal"` | `"premier league chelsea vs arsenal"` (cross-year season stripped) |

All events within the same F1 race weekend must produce identical group strings. The `compute_event_sequences()` function groups by this string and assigns the same sequence to each session, so they share episode number ranges (e.g. Australian GP session 1 → episodes 111–150, Monaco GP session 2 → episodes 211–250).
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: derive_weekend_group() now strips leading year tokens and dash-separated session suffixes before inline keyword cleanup. Added numbering regression coverage.

title: [bug] episode_display_title returns raw TheSportsDB event name including year and competition prefix
description:
`episode_display_title(segment, event)` in `provider/items.py` returns `event.name` verbatim for any segment whose `kind` is in `PRIMARY_EVENT_KINDS = {"match", "race", "practice", "qualifying", "sprint", "sprint_qualifying"}`. TheSportsDB names events as e.g. `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"`, so Plex episode titles become `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` — redundant (year already shown by season, competition name already shown by show) and ugly.

The function has no access to the competition name, so it cannot strip it. The fix threads `competition_name` through.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/provider/items.py`

**Change 1 — add `import re` at the top** (not currently imported).

**Change 2 — add module-level regex constant** after the existing imports, before `PRIMARY_EVENT_KINDS`:
```python
_YEAR_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}(?:/\d{2,4})?\s+")
```

**Change 3 — add new helper function** directly before `episode_display_title`:
```python
def _strip_event_name_prefixes(event_name: str, competition_name: str) -> str:
    """Strip leading year token and competition name prefix from TheSportsDB-style event names.

    Examples:
      "2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying", "Formula 1"
        -> "Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"
      "2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix", "Formula 1"
        -> "Australian Grand Prix"
      "Liverpool vs Arsenal", "Premier League"
        -> "Liverpool vs Arsenal"  (no prefix to strip)
      "Austrian Grand Prix Qualifying", "Formula 1"
        -> "Austrian Grand Prix Qualifying"  (no year prefix, no competition prefix)
    """
    # Strip leading "YYYY " or "YYYY/YY " year token
    text = _YEAR_PREFIX_RE.sub("", event_name).strip()
    # Strip competition name prefix (case-insensitive)
    comp_lower = competition_name.lower().strip()
    if comp_lower and text.lower().startswith(comp_lower):
        text = text[len(competition_name):].lstrip(" -–").strip()
    # Guard: never return empty string
    return text or event_name
```

**Change 4 — update `episode_display_title` signature and body:**

Old signature:
```python
def episode_display_title(segment: Segment, event: Event | None) -> str:
```
New signature (add `competition_name` with default so existing callers outside this file won't break if any exist, though the only real caller is `episode_metadata()` which is in the same file):
```python
def episode_display_title(segment: Segment, event: Event | None, competition_name: str = "") -> str:
```

Old body (lines 58–66):
```python
    if event is None or not event.name:
        return segment.title
    if segment.kind in PRIMARY_EVENT_KINDS:
        return event.name
    event_tokens = normalize_title(event.name)
    segment_tokens = normalize_title(segment.title)
    if segment_tokens[: len(event_tokens)] == event_tokens:
        return segment.title
    return f"{event.name} {segment.title}".strip()
```
New body:
```python
    if event is None or not event.name:
        return segment.title
    if segment.kind in PRIMARY_EVENT_KINDS:
        return _strip_event_name_prefixes(event.name, competition_name)
    event_tokens = normalize_title(event.name)
    segment_tokens = normalize_title(segment.title)
    if segment_tokens[: len(event_tokens)] == event_tokens:
        return segment.title
    stripped_event = _strip_event_name_prefixes(event.name, competition_name)
    return f"{stripped_event} {segment.title}".strip()
```
Note: the non-PRIMARY branch also uses the stripped event name (last line) so that e.g. "highlights" segments don't also get the verbose "2025 Formula 1 ..." prefix.

**Change 5 — update the call in `episode_metadata()`** (the only caller inside this file, ~line 96):

Old:
```python
        title=episode_display_title(segment, event),
```
New:
```python
        title=episode_display_title(segment, event, competition.name),
```
`competition` is already a parameter of `episode_metadata()` so no further changes needed.

**`episode_display_title` is also called from `match_service.py`** (via `SportScanner-5k6` fix). That call will also need to pass `competition.name`. See that bead.

**Verification:**
| event.name | competition.name | kind | expected title |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` | `"Formula 1"` | `"qualifying"` | `"Australian Grand Prix - Qualifying"` |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix"` | `"Formula 1"` | `"race"` | `"Australian Grand Prix"` |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix - Free Practice 1"` | `"Formula 1"` | `"practice"` | `"Australian Grand Prix - Free Practice 1"` |
| `"Austrian Grand Prix Qualifying"` | `"Formula 1"` | `"qualifying"` | `"Austrian Grand Prix Qualifying"` (no year, no F1 prefix — unchanged; existing tests pass) |
| `"Liverpool vs Arsenal"` | `"Premier League"` | `"match"` | `"Liverpool vs Arsenal"` (no prefix match) |
| `"2025 Formula 1 Australian Grand Prix"` | `"Formula 1"` | `"highlights"` | `"Australian Grand Prix Highlights"` (non-PRIMARY path, stripped event + segment.title) |
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: threaded competition_name through episode_display_title(), stripped TheSportsDB year/competition prefixes, and reused the cleaned event name in non-primary titles. Added provider regression coverage.

title: [bug] Competition name matching fails for 'Formula 1' vs 'Formula 1 World Championship'
description:
`SequenceMatcher(None, "formula 1", "formula 1 world championship").ratio()` ≈ 0.70, below the hardcoded 0.80 threshold used in both `best_db_competition_match` and `best_upstream_competition_match`. When a file with `show="Formula 1"` is ingested, competition resolution fails to find the TheSportsDB competition ("Formula 1 World Championship"), so a `manual_formula-1` Competition is created with no `tsdb_id`. Without a `tsdb_id`, `_populate_season_events()` returns immediately (early-exit guard: `if competition.tsdb_id is None: return False`), so no Events are ever loaded from TheSportsDB for that season — all segments end up in REVIEW. Also affects the `match_event()` search filter which uses a separate 0.70 threshold.

**File:** `src/sportscanner/organizer/matcher.py`

**Change 1 — add `import re` at the top** (it is not currently imported in this file).

**Change 2 — add normalization constant and helper after `similarity()`:**
```python
_COMPETITION_NOISE_SUFFIXES = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:world\s+championship|championship|series)\s*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

def _normalize_competition_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Strip trailing noise words that vary between short/long competition names.
    'Formula 1 World Championship' -> 'Formula 1'
    'Bundesliga' -> 'Bundesliga' (no change)
    Never returns empty string — falls back to original.
    """
    normalized = _COMPETITION_NOISE_SUFFIXES.sub("", name).strip()
    return normalized or name
```

**Do NOT strip 'league', 'cup', 'premier'** — those are meaningful parts of competition names (Premier League, FA Cup). Only strip "world championship", "championship", "series".

**Change 3 — rewrite `best_db_competition_match`** (lower default threshold 0.80 → 0.75, add normalized scoring):
```python
def best_db_competition_match(query: str, competitions: Iterable[Competition], threshold: float = 0.75) -> Competition | None:
    normalized_query = _normalize_competition_name(query)
    best_score = 0.0
    best_competition: Competition | None = None
    for competition in competitions:
        for name in competition.all_names():
            raw_score = similarity(query, name)
            norm_score = similarity(normalized_query, _normalize_competition_name(name))
            score = max(raw_score, norm_score)
            if score > best_score:
                best_score = score
                best_competition = competition
    if best_score >= threshold:
        return best_competition
    return None
```

**Change 4 — rewrite `best_upstream_competition_match`** (lower default threshold 0.80 → 0.75, add normalized scoring):
```python
def best_upstream_competition_match(
    query: str,
    competitions: Iterable[UpstreamCompetition],
    threshold: float = 0.75,
) -> CompetitionMatch | None:
    normalized_query = _normalize_competition_name(query)
    best: CompetitionMatch | None = None
    for competition in competitions:
        names = [competition.name, *competition.alternate_names]
        score = max(
            max(similarity(query, n) for n in names if n),
            max(similarity(normalized_query, _normalize_competition_name(n)) for n in names if n),
        )
        if best is None or score > best.confidence:
            best = CompetitionMatch(
                name=competition.name,
                competition_id=competition.id,
                tsdb_id=competition.tsdb_id,
                confidence=score,
                source="upstream",
            )
    if best is None or best.confidence < threshold:
        return None
    return best
```

**Change 5 — update `match_event()` competition filter** (lower 0.70 → 0.60, add normalized path):

Find the line `if not item.competition_name or similarity(normalized_show, item.competition_name.lower()) >= 0.7` and replace with:
```python
normalized_show = parsed.show.lower()
normalized_show_n = _normalize_competition_name(parsed.show).lower()
filtered_search = [
    item for item in search_results
    if not item.competition_name or max(
        similarity(normalized_show, item.competition_name.lower()),
        similarity(normalized_show_n, _normalize_competition_name(item.competition_name).lower()),
    ) >= 0.6
]
```

**Verification:**
- `_normalize_competition_name("Formula 1 World Championship")` → `"Formula 1"`
- `_normalize_competition_name("Premier League")` → `"Premier League"` (unchanged — "league" not in strip list)
- `_normalize_competition_name("FA Cup")` → `"FA Cup"` (unchanged)
- `_normalize_competition_name("UCI World Championship Series")` → `"UCI"` — acceptable; these rarely appear as show names
- `best_upstream_competition_match("Formula 1", [UpstreamCompetition(name="Formula 1 World Championship")])` → returns the competition (was: returned None)
- `best_db_competition_match("Formula 1", [Competition(name="Formula 1 World Championship")])` → returns the competition (was: returned None)

**Regression risk:** Lowering from 0.80 to 0.75 could produce false positives for similar-sounding competitions (e.g. "Ligue 1" matching "Ligue 2"). The normalized-comparison path only fires when the raw comparison also misses, so the blast radius is limited to cases where the raw similarity is between 0.75–0.80. Accept this trade-off.
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: normalized competition matching by stripping trailing world championship/championship/series, lowered thresholds as discussed, and applied the normalized path to DB/upstream competition matching plus event-search filtering. Added matcher regressions.

title: [bug] SEGMENT_KIND_MAP ordering causes 'Sprint Race' to match as 'race' instead of 'sprint'
description:
Dict iterates in insertion order. 'race' key appears at position 3 of SEGMENT_KIND_MAP, before 'sprint race' is defined at all. So `infer_segment_kind(None, "Sprint Race")` iterates keys, finds "race" as a substring of "sprint race", and returns "race" instead of "sprint".

**File:** `src/sportscanner/organizer/parser.py`

**Exact function affected:** `infer_segment_kind()` (line ~104). It does `if key in lowered: return value` — first match wins, so key order is critical.

**Fix:** Replace the entire `SEGMENT_KIND_MAP` dict with the following. Ordering rules: multi-word compound keys before their component single words; more-specific before less-specific.

```python
SEGMENT_KIND_MAP = {
    # Multi-word sprint sessions — must come before bare "race" and bare "sprint"
    "sprint race": "sprint",
    "sprint qualifying": "sprint_qualifying",
    "shootout qualifying": "sprint_qualifying",
    # Explicit free-practice forms — before bare "practice"
    "free practice 1": "practice",
    "free practice 2": "practice",
    "free practice 3": "practice",
    "fp1": "practice",
    "fp2": "practice",
    "fp3": "practice",
    "practice 1": "practice",
    "practice 2": "practice",
    "practice 3": "practice",
    "practice": "practice",
    # Primary session types — after all multi-word forms above
    "qualifying": "qualifying",
    "qual": "qualifying",
    "sprint": "sprint",
    "race": "race",
    "main event": "race",
    "match": "match",
    "game": "match",
    # Editorial / non-live
    "pregame": "pregame",
    "pre game": "pregame",
    "pre-race show": "pregame",
    "postgame": "postgame",
    "post game": "postgame",
    "post-race analysis": "analysis",
    "analysis": "analysis",
    "highlights": "highlights",
    "condensed": "condensed",
    "condensed game": "condensed",
    "alternate feed": "alt_feed",
    "alt feed": "alt_feed",
    "alt": "alt_feed",
}
```

**No other code changes required** — `infer_segment_kind()` body itself is unchanged; only the dict contents change.

**Verification — assert all of these:**
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Sprint Race")` → `"sprint"` (was `"race"` — the core bug)
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Sprint Qualifying")` → `"sprint_qualifying"` (unchanged)
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Free Practice 1")` → `"practice"` (unchanged, now explicit key)
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Race")` → `"race"` (unchanged)
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Qualifying")` → `"qualifying"` (unchanged)
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Sprint")` → `"sprint"` (unchanged; "sprint qualifying" won't match bare "Sprint" because "sprint qualifying" is not a substring of "sprint")
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Austrian Grand Prix Sprint Race")` → `"sprint"` (substring "sprint race" matches before "race")
- `infer_segment_kind(None, "Austrian Grand Prix Race")` → `"race"` (no "sprint race" substring)
notes: 2026-03-12 implementation: reordered SEGMENT_KIND_MAP so sprint/practice compound phrases win before bare race/sprint/practice keys. Added parser regression coverage.
